articles.title: GRSE Emerges Lowest Bidder For Energy Major's Platform Supply Vessel Tender Worth ₹1,032 Crore
articles.description: State-owned Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Ltd has emerged as the lowest bidder in a landmark commercial shipbuilding tender floated by Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Ltd, ET Infra reported.The tender, which is the first to be finalised after the Union Cabinet approved a ₹69,725 crore package to promote domestic shipbuilding, involves the construction of four Platform Supply Vessels.

articles.title: PM Vishwakarma and PMMY Boost MSMEs in West Bengal
articles.description: PM Vishwakarma scheme was launched on 17.09.2023 to provide end-to-end holistic support to artisans and craftspeople of 18 traditional trades who work with their hands and tools. The scheme covers 18 trades, namely Carpenter, Boat Maker, Armourer, Metal Artisan, Tool Kit Maker, Locksmith, Goldsmith, Potter, Sculptor/Stone Worker, Cobbler/Footwear Artisan, Mason, Basket/Mat/Broom Maker, Toy Maker (Traditional), Barber, Garland Maker, Washerman, Tailor and Fishing Net Maker. The implementation of PM Vishwakarma has commenced in the State of West Bengal following the issuance of a notification by the Government of West Bengal constituting the State Monitoring Committee and District Implementation Committees on 14.05.2026 for the roll-out of the Scheme in the State. Under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY), a total of 5.82 crore loans amounting to Rs. 3.55 lakh crore have been disbursed since inception i.e. 08.04.2015 till 26.06.2026 in the State of West Bengal. The Government has undertaken the following initiatives for potential women beneficiaries throughout the country including Sundarbans-based women entrepreneurs and fisherfolk: Udyam Registration Portal (UR) and Udyam Assist Portal (UAP): women owned enterprises registered are eligible to avail benefits under various schemes of the Ministry including access to Priority Sector Lending. Public Procurement Policy for MSEs: Central Ministries and CPSEs are mandated to procure atleast 3% of their annual procurement from women owned Micro and Small Enterprises, thereby facilitating market access. Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE): women owned Micro and Small Enterprises are eligible for enhanced guarantee coverage of upto 90% (as against 75% for others) and a 10% concession in the annual guarantee fee. PMEGP: Women beneficiaries are categorized under Special Category and eligible for a higher Margin Money (MM) Subsidy rate of upto 35% and lower own contribution of 5% of project cost, compared to 25% MM Subsidy rate and 10% own contribution of project cost for beneficiaries under General category. Skill Upgradation and Mahila Coir Yojana: Women artisans engaged in the coir sector are provided with skill upgradation training under the Coir Vikas Yojana to enhance their employability and entrepreneurial capabilities. Procurement and Marketing Support (PMS) Scheme: women entrepreneurs are provided financial assistance of upto 100% of the admissible expenditure for participation in domestic trade fairs, compared to 80% for other entrepreneurs. PM Vishwakarma Scheme: women artisans engaged in any of the 18 notified trades are eligible for benefits including skill training, toolkit incentive, collateral free credit support, incentive for digital transactions and marketing support. Yashasvini Campaign: Ministry undertakes awareness, handholding, mentorship and capacity building activities to facilitate access of existing and aspiring women entrepreneurs to various Government schemes and institutional support. The Incubation Component of the MSME Innovative Scheme of the Ministry of MSME is aimed at promoting innovation, support new ideas, and facilitate the transformation of concepts into viable business ventures. It plays a crucial role in strengthening the MSME and thus, start-up ecosystem by nurturing early-stage ideas. It supports the process of incubation through Host Institutes (HI), which are academic institutions and Innovation centers acting as Business Incubators (BI) across the country. Currently, there are 23 Host Institutes (HI) in West Bengal and each approved idea is eligible for financial support of up to a maximum amount of Rs. 15 lakh.

articles.title: Ranchi High Court's Campus To Use Solar For Its Carport Soon
articles.description: The Jharkhand Renewable Energy Development Agency (JREDA) has invited bids for the design, engineering, supply, installation, testing and commissioning of a 1.2 MW grid-connected solar carport power plant at the New High Court campus in Ranchi, as part of the state's efforts to expand solar infrastructure at government institutions. The project also includes a five-year comprehensive maintenance contract (CMC) and will be executed on a turnkey basis. The tender, carrying an estimated project cost of approximately ₹11.8 crore (excluding GST), covers the installation of the solar carport across four locations within the High Court premises. The selected developer will be required to complete the project within six months, while the overall contract period has been fixed at five years and six months. On an expansion spree According to the bid document, the proposed installation is an expansion of an existing 2 MW solar carport system already operational at the New High Court complex. JREDA has specified that the new facility must match the existing installation in terms of symmetry, configuration, design and technical specifications to maintain uniformity across the campus. The agency has prescribed key equipment specifications for the project. The solar modules are to be 500 Wp or higher mono-crystalline modules compliant with the latest MNRE ALMM requirements, while bidders have been directed to supply carport structures compatible with the existing installation. The project scope also includes inverters, SCADA and weather monitoring systems, electrical balance-of-system components, and a dedicated monitoring workstation. The project will be funded by the Government of Jharkhand and implemented through JREDA. For general bidders, the tender requires an earnest money deposit (EMD) of ₹23.6 lakh, while the tender fee has been fixed at ₹10,000. Registered manufacturing-sector micro and small enterprises (MSEs) based in Jharkhand have been exempted from both the tender fee and EMD under the state's procurement policy, subject to eligibility conditions. Eligibility Criteria Eligibility criteria require bidders to have prior experience in designing and commissioning grid-connected solar carport projects. General bidders must have completed one project worth at least 80% of the estimated project value, or two projects of at least 50% each, or three projects worth at least 40% each during the previous seven years. The completed installations must have remained operational for at least six months before bid submission. JREDA has scheduled the pre-bid meeting for July 13, while online bids will be accepted until July 29. Technical bids are slated to be opened on July 31. The tender also states that the contract will be awarded to the lowest (L1) bidder, with allocations to eligible Jharkhand-based MSEs to be made in accordance with the state's procurement policy wherever applicable. This project further expands the deployment of solar-powered parking infrastructure in Jharkhand, leveraging otherwise unused parking spaces to generate renewable electricity while providing covered parking for vehicles.
